title: `explode` keeps a row for a NULL list and drops an empty list
verdict: a NULL list gives a NULL row, `[]` no row; `keep_nulls=False` drops the NULL row too
description: `explode` gives one row per element, one NULL row for a NULL list and no row for an empty list (the defaults `empty_as_null=False, keep_nulls=True`). With `keep_nulls=False` a NULL list gives no row either, which is SQL's `UNNEST`; `empty_as_null=True` gives an empty list a NULL row.
reference: `UNNEST`: one row per element, none for an empty list or NULL.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.

explode calls the eager `DataFrame.explode`, in memory; s-explode explodes 6000 rows lazily on each engine, with and without `empty_as_null=False, keep_nulls=False`: the same rows in the same order (6000 and 4500).

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: empty list: NULL row only if empty_as_null; NULL list: NULL row only if keep_nulls; else dropped
streaming: Explode is streamable and runs as a Map node calling the in-memory evaluate_function_ir per morsel
empty_as_null and keep_nulls documented; defaults False and True
test_explode_params: [[1,2,3], None, [4,5,6], []] under all four flag pairs (in-memory)
LazyFrame({'i':[1,2,3,4],'l':[[1,2],[],None,[None]]}).explode('l') on in-memory and streaming (morsel 64): [(1,1),(1,2),(3,None),(4,None)]; the empty list gives no row by default

provenance.notes: Corrected the description: it said the default gives a NULL row for an empty list. At 2.1.0 the default `empty_as_null=False` gives no row for an empty list (the probe explode shows it too) and one NULL row for a NULL list.
